gaps.lead: I only understood the pattern much later.
gaps.explanation: Front 'only + time phrase' forces inversion: Only much later did I understand.

gaps.lead: 'You mustn't run near the pool,' the lifeguard told the children.
gaps.sentence: The lifeguard told the children ___ near the pool.

gaps.lead: Even though she was exhausted after twelve hours on duty, the surgeon completed the operation.
gaps.sentence: ___ exhausted after twelve hours on duty, the surgeon completed the operation.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though she was' becomes 'in spite of being' — concession + gerund.

gaps.lead: Do you mind if I come over to see you later?
gaps.sentence: Do you ___ coming over to see you later?
gaps.explanation: 'Have any objection to me/my coming' is the formal equivalent of 'do you mind'.

gaps.lead: People claim that this herbal tea cures colds.
gaps.explanation: X is claimed to + infinitive = people claim X does.

gaps.lead: It was unfair of the referee to send him off.
gaps.explanation: should(n't) have + participle criticises a past decision.
